title: Review: Momentum and its conservation; Impulse and force–time graphs; Work done
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D09-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; E01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D09-1#N.16a, D10-1#N.12, E01-1#N.5, D09-1#N.10a, D10-1#N.4a, E01-1#N.9b, D09-1#N.7, D09-1#N.2. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Momentum
items.clue: Vector equal to mass × velocity, measured in kg m s⁻¹.

items.label: Newton's third law
items.clue: Reason two colliding bodies push each other with equal and opposite forces.

items.label: Component
items.clue: Part of a force along the displacement: the only part that transfers energy.

items.label: Crumple zone
items.clue: Car feature that lengthens the stopping time, making the average force smaller.

questions.stem: A person of mass 60 kg stands in a rowing boat of mass 120 kg. Both are at rest, and water resistance is negligible. The person jumps horizontally from the boat onto a jetty, leaving at 1.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the boat immediately afterwards is correct?

options.text: It moves away from the jetty at 1.0 m s⁻¹, as the forces on the person and the boat are equal and opposite.
It stays at rest, as the person pushes off towards the jetty and not against the boat.
It moves away at 0.50 m s⁻¹, with the same kinetic energy as the person.
It moves away at 0.50 m s⁻¹, with momentum equal and opposite to the person's.

questions.stem: Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed

questions.stem: A worker uses a rope to lower a box straight down at constant speed. Which statement about the work done on the box during the descent is correct?

options.text: The tension does positive work and gravity does negative work on the box.
The tension does negative work and gravity does positive work.
The tension and gravity both do positive work on the box as it moves.
Neither force does any work, as the box's speed does not change.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg trolley moving at 5.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a 3.0 kg trolley at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg trolley moves backwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹ and the 3.0 kg trolley moves forwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?

A sledge on level snow is pulled horizontally with a constant force of 60.0 N for 4.00 s. Throughout this time it slides forwards and the frictional force on it is 22.0 N. What is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the sledge by the resultant force during the 4.00 s?

options.text: 240 N s
328 N s
9.5 N s
152 N s

questions.explanation: Resultant force = 60.0 − 22.0 = 38.0 N. J = FΔt = 38.0 × 4.00 = 152 N s, forwards.

questions.stem: A student carries a bag of weight 15 N up a flight of stairs at constant velocity. The bag moves 4.0 m horizontally and rises 3.0 m, so it travels 5.0 m along the stairs. How much work does the student's upward force do on the bag?

options.text: 60 J, the upward force multiplied by the horizontal distance.
45 J, the upward force multiplied by the height gained.
75 J, the upward force multiplied by the distance along the stairs.
Zero, as the bag moves at constant velocity, so no work is done on it.

questions.explanation: The force is vertical and the displacement is 5.0 m at an angle θ to it, with cos θ = 3.0/5.0. Work = 15 × 5.0 × 0.60 = 45 J: the force times the 3.0 m rise.

questions.stem: Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.

questions.stem: A cricket ball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?
